form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Leahy (for himself, Mr. Cornyn, and Mr. Tillis) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary

form.official-title: To amend title 35, United States Code, to address matters relating to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board of the United States Patent and Trademark Office, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Patent Trial and Appeal Board Reform Act of 2022.

subsection.text: Title 35, United States Code, is amended—

paragraph.text: in section 6—

subparagraph.text: in subsection (a), by inserting after the third sentence the following: Each member of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board shall comply with the Code of Conduct for United States Judges, including limitations on ex parte communications, when performing the duties enumerated in subsection (b).;
in subsection (c)—

clause.text: in the second sentence, by striking Only the and inserting The; and

by adding at the end the following: After the constitution of a panel of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board under this subsection has been made public, any changes to the constitution of that panel, including changes that were made before the constitution of the panel was made public, shall be noted in the record.;

subparagraph.text: by redesignating subsection (d) as subsection (e);
by inserting after subsection (c) the following:
With respect to a decision of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board—

clause.text: the Director may, on the initiative of the Director, review, and modify or set aside, the decision;
if the decision is issued under section 318(a) or 328(a), a party to the applicable inter partes or post-grant review may request that the Director review, and modify or set aside, the decision; and

if the decision is issued under section 314 or 324 under a delegation by the Director, a party to the applicable inter partes or post-grant review petition may request that the Director review, and modify or set aside, the decision.

subparagraph.header: Effect of request for review of determination to institute review
subparagraph.text: A request for review under subparagraph (A)(iii) shall not be a basis to stay or delay any proceeding.
Any review by the Director under paragraph (1) shall be issued in a separate written opinion that—

clause.text: is made part of the public record;
sets forth the reasons for the review, modification, or setting aside of the decision of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board; and
may be designated as precedential, and if it is designated as precedential, shall be followed by future panels of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, unless and until the opinion is—

subclause.text: rescinded; or
superseded by—

item.text: a decision of the Director that is designated as precedential; or

subparagraph.text: Nothing in subparagraph (A)(iii) shall be construed to affect the obligation of the Director to prescribe regulations under section 316(a) or 326(a).

paragraph.text: Not later than 18 months after the date of enactment of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board Reform Act of 2022, the Director shall promulgate rules addressing the following issues:

subparagraph.text: With respect to review of a decision on the initiative of the Director under paragraph (1)(A)(i)—

clause.text: the timeline under which the Director may review the decision, which shall be consistent with the requirements under section 318(e) or 328(e), if applicable; and
the bases on which the Director may review the decision.

subparagraph.text: With respect to a request by a party under clause (ii) or (iii) of paragraph (1)(A)—

clause.text: the timeline for submitting such a request;
the content that the party is required to include in such a request;
the bases on which the party may submit such a request; and
the timeline for any response or reply to such a request such that the request can be decided within the deadline imposed under section 318(e) or 328(e), as applicable.

paragraph.header: Determination whether to review final decisions of Board
paragraph.text: Notwithstanding the bases for review promulgated under paragraph (3), the determination whether to review a final decision of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board under this subsection is committed to the discretion of the Director.

For the purposes of an appeal permitted under section 141, any decision on review of a final written decision of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board under section 318(a) or 328(a), that is issued by the Director under this subsection, shall be deemed a final written decision of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board.

paragraph.text: If new or amended claims issue from reexamination after the petitioner, real party in interest, or privy of the petitioner is served with the complaint, an inter partes review of those claims, and any dependent claims depending from those claims, may be instituted if the petition requesting the review is filed not later than 1 year after the date on which the new or amended claims are asserted against the petitioner, real party in interest, or privy of the petitioner.

subsection.header: Institution not To be denied based on parallel proceedings
subsection.text: In deciding whether to institute an inter partes review proceeding, the Director shall not in any respect consider an ongoing civil action or a proceeding before the International Trade Commission under section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1337), other than with respect to—

paragraph.text: the bars specified in subsections (a) and (b); or
the determination under section 314(a) that there is a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least 1 of the claims challenged in the petition.

subsection.text: Not later than 120 days after the date on which the Patent Trial and Appeal Board issues a final written decision under subsection (a), the Board or the Director shall finally decide any request for reconsideration, rehearing, or review that is submitted with respect to the decision, except that the Director may, for good cause shown, extend that 120-day period by not more than 60 days.

subsection.text: For the purposes of an appeal described in subsection (a), the right to appeal shall extend at least to any dissatisfied party that reasonably expects that another person will assert estoppel against the party under section 315(e) as a result of the decision.

Not later than 120 days after the date on which a mandate issues from the court remanding to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board after an appeal under subsection (a), the Board or the Director shall finally decide any issue on remand, except that the Director may, for good cause shown, extend that 120-day period by not more than 60 days.

subparagraph.text: by adding at the end the following:

section.header: Support for small and micro entities in inter partes review and post-grant review

subsection.text: In this section, the term covered patent means a patent—

paragraph.text: that is the subject of a petition for inter partes review under chapter 31 or post-grant review under chapter 32;
whose owner at the time of the patent application qualified for small entity or micro entity status;
whose owner, on the date on which the petition is filed, would qualify for small entity or micro entity status if that owner were to file a patent application;
whose owner has not asserted the patent in litigation;
that has not been licensed to any other party that would not qualify for small entity or micro entity status if that party were to file a patent application; and
the owner or exclusive licensee of which makes or uses the claimed invention in a commercial enterprise, or has made substantial preparations to do so.

The Office shall pay to the owner of a covered patent all of the reasonable expenses of the proceeding actually incurred by the patent owner (and not expenses incurred by a third party funding the proceeding), including reasonable expert witness fees and reasonable attorney fees, for defending the inter partes review or post-grant review.
The expenses to be paid under paragraph (1) shall include expenses of—

subparagraph.text: a preliminary response under section 313 or 323;
a response under section 316(a)(8) or 326(a)(8);
any discovery under section 316(a)(5) or 326(a)(5);
motions filed at the Patent Trial and Appeal Board;
any requests for reconsideration, rehearing, or review; and
any proceedings after a remand from the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.

paragraph.text: The Office shall pay reasonable expenses under paragraph (1) regardless of the outcome of the proceeding.
The expenses to be paid under paragraph (1) shall not include expenses incurred—

subparagraph.text: in a proceeding at the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit or any tribunal outside the Office; or
in moving to amend any patent claim under—

clause.text: subsection (a)(9), (d), or (e) of section 316; or
subsection (a)(9), (d), or (e) of section 326.

subsection.text: The total estimated expenses paid to owners of covered patents under this section—

paragraph.text: shall be considered part of the aggregate costs under section 311(a) or 321(a); and
shall be recovered through fees paid by petitioners.

In determining whether to institute or order a proceeding under this chapter, chapter 30, or chapter 31, the Director may take into account whether, and reject the petition or request because, the same or substantially the same prior art or arguments previously were presented to the Office.
